analysis.one_liner: Godrej Consumer Products makes household and personal-care staples - soaps, hair colour, air fresheners, insecticides - sold mainly in India, Indonesia, Africa and Latin America.
analysis.whats_happening: The board meets on October 29, 2026 (within two weeks) to approve Q2 FY27 (July-Sept 2026) results. Ahead of that, a pre-results business update on October 5, 2026 flagged consolidated revenue growth in the high teens, volume growth in high single digits and double-digit EBITDA growth for the quarter, though standalone India is said to carry a 100-150 bps hit from 'trade inventory correction.' The stock rose about 2% on this update. Separately, the company opened the first phase of a new ~Rs 250 crore manufacturing facility in Indonesia on October 6, 2026, adding roughly 15% home-and-personal-care capacity there.
analysis.plain_terms: This is a well-known FMCG household name, but the stock has fallen 41.5% from its September 2024 high and sits close to its 52-week low even as management describes the underlying business as still growing. The last fully reported quarter (Jul-Sep 2025) showed sales up only 4% and profit before exceptionals down 2%, while the Personal Care segment fell because of a GST-related tax transition, not necessarily weaker demand. The tension to hold in mind: volumes are still growing, but the stock trades at a much richer multiple than peers, so the market is pricing in more than the recent numbers have delivered.
analysis.quarters: Q2 FY26 (Jul-Sep 2025, reported Nov 2025): consolidated sales +4% YoY to about Rs 3,802 crore, volume +3%, EBITDA margin 19.3%, PAT before exceptionals down 2%. Home Care (air fresheners, fabric care) grew 6%; Personal Care fell 2%, which management linked to the GST transition affecting soaps - treat this revenue line as not strictly comparable and look at EBITDA/PAT instead. Indonesia fell 7% in constant currency on pricing pressure; Africa/US/Middle East grew 25% in INR (15% constant currency). Full-year FY26 guidance was high-single-digit India volume growth and double-digit India EBITDA growth. For the quarter about to be reported (Q2 FY27, ended Sep 2026), the October 5, 2026 pre-results update points to a sharp pickup - high-teens revenue growth, high-single-digit volumes, double-digit EBITDA growth - but this is management's preliminary estimate, not the audited number, which lands October 29, 2026.
analysis.performance_read: The stock is down 41.5% from its September 2024 peak of Rs 1,460.97 and trades near its 52-week low (Rs 837 vs last close Rs 855). All three historical stock splits (2006, 2017, 2018) are already reflected in the return history and there has been no recent demerger of this entity, so this decline is a genuine erosion of shareholder value, not a corporate-action artifact. Returns of -22.2% (1Y), -9.7% (3Y) and -11.5% (5Y) badly lag the Nifty (+25.3% over 5Y), though GCPL has held up better than peer Dabur, which is down a steeper 33.4% over 5 years. The underperformance has worsened recently: -19.8% over just the last 3 months versus -4.9% for the Nifty.
analysis.valuation_read: P/E estimates from different sources cluster around 46-55x, with one outlier near 69x (likely using a non-comparable trailing EPS base) set aside. Either way, this sits well above the household and personal-care industry median P/E of roughly 30x, and P/B is around 7x. Why it looks expensive: the market is still paying up for GCPL's brand strength and 25% ROCE plus optionality in Indonesia, Africa and Latin America. Whether it is actually cheap depends on whether the double-digit EBITDA growth flagged for the Sept 2026 quarter materialises - profit growth has lagged revenue growth in recent reported quarters, so the premium is not yet backed by matching profit momentum.
analysis.growth_read: Growth has stayed volume-led rather than purely price-led - 3% volume growth in the last reported quarter, with India ex-soaps growing in double digits, and high-single-digit volume growth guided for the quarter about to be reported. But margin expansion has not kept pace: PAT before exceptionals fell 2% in the last reported quarter even as revenue rose 4%, weighed down by Indonesia weakness and the GST-driven Personal Care decline.
analysis.health_read: Debt-to-equity of about 0.32 and ROCE near 25% point to a balance sheet that isn't under financial strain. Not verified - check on Screener for the operating-cash-flow-to-PAT conversion ratio. On the information available, the risk here looks more like business risk - consumption softness, Indonesia pricing pressure, GST transition noise - than balance-sheet or financial risk.
analysis.ownership_read: The Godrej family (promoters) held 53.05% as of June 2026, unchanged after an internal block deal between promoter-group entities on September 24, 2026. Reported promoter pledge is 0% as of June 2026 (down from 0.79% in March 2025), though a separate, non-lending encumbrance from a March 2020 Shareholders' Agreement still sits on shares held by three family members (Burjis, Sohrab and Hormazd Godrej) - this is a family-governance restriction, not a pledge against debt. FIIs hold 12.33%, DIIs 19.59% (including mutual funds at 10.76%), and public shareholders 15.03%. No marquee individual investor turned up in the shareholding data searched; if one is expected, they are not evidently on the register.
strengths: Volume growth stayed positive at 3% even in a soft quarter, with India ex-soaps posting double-digit volume growth
ROCE of about 25% is well above the household/personal-care sector median of roughly 19%
Low leverage (debt-to-equity ~0.32) left room to fund the Rs 289 crore Muuchstac acquisition and the ~Rs 250 crore Indonesia capacity expansion without strain
Home Care (air fresheners, fabric care) grew 6% in the last reported quarter, a clear bright spot against Personal Care weakness
watchpoints: Valuation sits at a P/E cluster of roughly 46-55x versus an industry median near 30x, pricing in more than recent results have delivered
Indonesia, a meaningful slice of international sales, declined 7% in constant currency in the last reported quarter on pricing pressure
The Personal Care/soaps revenue decline is partly a GST-transition accounting effect flagged by management - not strictly comparable to prior periods
Standalone India business flagged a 100-150 bps hit from 'trade inventory correction' for the Sept 2026 quarter - worth watching whether this is one-off destocking or softer underlying demand
analysis.one_thing: The October 29, 2026 Q2 FY27 results - specifically whether the double-digit EBITDA growth flagged in the October 5 pre-results update actually comes through, especially outside India - is what will show whether the current premium valuation is justified.
analysis.data_notes: Q2 FY26 results cross-checked across Yahoo Finance, MarketScreener, Kalkine and Scanx coverage. Valuation metrics cross-checked across Eulerpool, Gurufocus and Tijori; P/E figures ranged from about 46x to 69x - the 69x outlier (Eulerpool) was set aside as likely using a non-comparable EPS base, and the 46-55x cluster was used instead. Shareholding and pledge data taken from Trendlyne. Could not verify exact current EPS, book value per share, or operating-cash-flow-to-PAT conversion - check these directly on Screener.
